decided_by: `michael-the-architect` rules ('Ask whether the premise runs', 'Measure, don't read', 'A remedy you propose is a claim', and 'A finding being real does not make its proposed fix right'); Pi 1.5.2 `dist/core/agent-session.js:2756-2828,3468-3500` and `dist/core/session-manager.js:256-275,1074-1084`.
answer:
1. **Confirmed.** My `michael-validate.json` finding 1 remedy (`await session.navigateTree(userEntryId)` then asserting `projectedToolResult` carries `BIG_TEXT`) fails as written. I checked `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.js:3468-3500`, `tests/app/extension/archive-session.test.ts:226-243` (`833f16c`), and ran both calls in a `mktemp -d` copy under vitest:
   - After `await session.prompt("run it")` settles, `session.sessionManager.getBranch()` is `["model_change", "thinking_level_change", "message:system", "message:user", "message:assistant" (toolUse), "message:toolResult", "message:assistant" ("done"), "custom:taiknr-side-store", "context_edit"]` (note `agent_before_settle` appends `taiknr-side-store` and `context_edit` after the second `assistant` message).
   - Calling `await session.navigateTree(userId, { summarize: false })` hits the `role === "user"` branch at `agent-session.js:3468-3470` (`newLeafId = targetEntry.parentId`), leaving `getBranch()` as `["model_change", "thinking_level_change", "message:system"]` — dropping both `user` and `toolResult` off the branch so `projectedToolResult(session)` is `undefined`.
   - Calling `await session.navigateTree(toolResultId, { summarize: false })` (`11.5` in `833f16c`) hits `agent-session.js:3477` (`newLeafId = targetId`), leaving `getBranch()` ending at `message:toolResult` (excluding `taiknr-side-store` and `context_edit`) and projecting the 700-char `BIG_TEXT` plus `IMAGE`. I had lifted Judge Gen's WARNING 1 recommendation verbatim without checking the branch or running the 5-line case, violating both "Ask whether the premise runs" and "A finding being real does not make its proposed fix right".

2. **Re-check of the other two `michael-validate.json` findings and every unrun remedy in this change:**
   - **`michael-validate.json` findings 2 and 3 (both clean):** Verified against `833f16c` (`npm run check` green, 16 files / 221 tests). Finding 2 deleted four trailing `(Trap N)` comment parentheticals on verified lines (`archived-output.ts:23`, `pi-archive-adapter.ts:64`, `session-start.ts:29`, `agent-before-settle.ts:52`) with no behavioral dependency. Finding 3 collapsed `LINE_SEPARATOR` and `LINE_SEPARATOR_ALL` into one `/\r\n|\r|\n|\u2028|\u2029|\u0085/g` constant in `archived-output.ts:24` — which I *had* measured in `node -e` (`re.lastIndex = 99` before `.split()` and `.replace()`) prior to proposing.
   - **Audit of all `propose_fix` remedies across `michael-resolve-s2.json`, `s3-r1..r5`, and `s5-r1..r4`:** Nothing currently live on the branch (`fc6e0a2`) has an unrunnable step, **but three earlier unrun remedies I wrote during the review loops had the exact same defect class** (each caught only because a subsequent council round flagged my own remedy):
     1. **`michael-resolve-s3-r1.json` → `structural-r1-ST-S3-1` (sub-bullet 2):** I proposed testing `setEnabled(false)` / `setEnabled(true)` mid-session inside `tests/app/extension/archive-session.test.ts`. That test loads `taiknr(pi)` as an extension factory where `const session = createSessionConfig()` (`src/app/extension/taiknr.ts:20`) is closure-private and `/taiknr` is out of scope (`D10`), so no handle existed to call `setEnabled` (caught by `critic-r2-CR-S3-R2-1`, fixed in `s3-r2` by moving `setEnabled` cases to handler-level `createGatedPi` tests).
     2. **`michael-resolve-s3-r2.json` → `critic-r2-CR-S3-R2-1` (sub-bullet 1b):** My replacement wording for `archive-session.test.ts` still asked to assert `'the archive empty'` and `'compaction hydration'` without `bindExtensions({ onError })`. `taiknr(pi)`'s `InMemoryArchiveStore` (`taiknr.ts:22`) is also closure-private with no reader until the recall card implements `context.ts` (and prototype spies violate the no-mocking-internals bar), and without `await session.bindExtensions({ onError })` (`agent-session.js:2756-2828`) `session_start` never fires in an SDK session (caught by `critic-r3-CR-S3-R3-1`, fixed in `s3-r3`).
     3. **`michael-resolve-s5-r1.json` → `readiness-s5r1-RD-S5-R1-2` / `ST-S5-R1-2`:** Pointing `7.1 boundary cases` at `7.2`'s `?? []` lookup-miss fallback asked for a test case that no `TurnEndEvent` can reach without mocking internal collaborators, because `toToolOutputCandidates` and `stageToolOutputs` derive `staged` from `event.toolResults` in the same call (caught by `readiness-s5r2-RD-S5-R2-1`, fixed in `s5-r2`).
     - By contrast, the two remedies I *did* run in `mktemp -d` before proposing (`RD-S5-R1-1` test counts and `RD-S5-R1-8` Group 10 session/abort/compaction recipes, which caught the 2-summary split-turn requirement and `sideIdx < keptIdx` ordering up front) landed cleanly on the first pass.

3. **What I will check before proposing any test remedy from now on:**
   - **Never copy a reviewer's suggested test fix unverified** (including on `minor` optional findings, where no later review round automatically guards my text).
   - **Check three preconditions against live source before writing a test remedy:** (a) **handle visibility** — every symbol/state the test calls or asserts on (`session`, `store`, `onError`) is reachable through that test file's actual wiring without new exports or internal spies; (b) **input reachability** — a real, unmocked public input can reach the branch being tested; and (c) **post-call state shape** — trace the exact state transition of every host call (`navigateTree`'s `user`-vs-non-`user` leaf rule, `compact`'s cut point, `abort`'s boundary skip).
   - **Run any non-model session/host test remedy in a `mktemp -d` copy before emitting the verdict** (`required_change_ran: true`), reserving `required_change_ran: false` strictly for steps that cannot run locally without spending a model call or touching external state.
